purpose: Define one owner-preserving system-to-system contract for every directed relationship among the nine current peer systems so operation semantics, database writes, events and errors cannot acquire duplicate owners.

COMMAND.owner_rule: Exactly one provider owns the command meaning and the resulting semantic state transition.
COMMAND.caller_rule: A caller may request the transition but never becomes co-owner and never writes the provider's semantic store.
COMMAND.concurrency_rule: Mutating commands require provider-defined idempotency and optimistic-version or equivalent conflict protection whenever replay or concurrency is possible.
COMMAND.database_rule: Only the provider may commit semantic writes to provider-owned state.

QUERY.owner_rule: Exactly one provider owns the queried semantic data and query meaning.
QUERY.caller_rule: Consumers obtain provider data through the query/API contract or an admitted projection, never by reading provider-private tables or schemas.
QUERY.side_effect_rule: A query may emit operational telemetry but may not change domain truth, admit evidence, authorize actions or perform external side effects.

API.owner_rule: The provider owns the synchronous contract surface.
API.semantic_rule: Every API operation resolves to COMMAND or QUERY semantics; API is transport/interface shape, not a third ownership model.
API.database_rule: An API cannot create shared database ownership or expose a peer-private write surface.

EVENT.owner_rule: Exactly one semantic owner publishes each event type after the owner has committed the fact it describes.
EVENT.consumer_rule: Subscribers may update only their own state in reaction. An event is a fact, not authority to mutate publisher state.
EVENT.delivery_rule: Consumers must tolerate at-least-once delivery and deduplicate by stable event identity where delivery can repeat.

ERROR.owner_rule: The provider owns typed errors for its operation namespace.
ERROR.consumer_rule: Consumers may map an error for presentation or their own facade, but must retain origin/provider identity and must not reinterpret the error as ownership transfer.
ERROR.database_rule: Errors never authorize compensating writes to another peer's semantic store.

operation_identity.domain_rule: DOMAIN must be a current capability module_key owned by PROVIDER in the selected crosswalk, or a current platform requirement id owned by PROVIDER.
operation_identity.registration_rule: Every public cross-peer operation must have one globally unique operation_id before implementation. Two providers may not register aliases for the same semantic operation.
operation_identity.transfer_rule: Moving an operation between providers is an architecture change requiring explicit migration; aliases may forward temporarily but may not create dual writers or dual semantic owners.

database_and_state_ownership.cross_peer_transaction_rule: No transaction may directly write semantic state for more than one peer. Each owner commits its own state; multi-peer workflows coordinate through commands, owner-local commits, events, idempotency and compensating/saga behavior.
database_and_state_ownership.projection_rule: A consumer may keep an owner-local read projection only from admitted QUERY/API/EVENT data with source owner, source version and provenance. The projection never becomes source-of-truth for the provider.
database_and_state_ownership.cache_rule: A cache is owned by the consuming system, is disposable, and may not become a second canonical writer. Invalidation follows provider version/event contracts.
database_and_state_ownership.backup_restore_rule: CORE may provide generic physical backup/restore mechanics; the semantic owner defines acceptance/currentness invariants for its records.

default_boundary.surface_rule: Only provider-owned registered operations and event/error namespaces are callable/consumable.

owns: CHAT/EXPECTATION/EXPERIENCE/LOCALAI product semantics assigned by the crosswalk
does_not_own: peer product semantics merely because CORE hosts transport, storage, transactions, scheduling or orchestration

owns: CURRICULUM capability under the frozen internal Curriculum boundary
remaining integration of preserved completed Prose capability

does_not_own: source peer semantic records merely because it calculates over them
the caller's Book, Learning, Documents or other peer semantic state merely because media is produced for it
peer semantic state used to formulate an external action
generic research execution infrastructure hosted by CORE
caller state changed after consuming research
another peer's canonical state merely because code is generated for it

learning_curriculum_experience_shared.rule: This split is frozen and must not be redesigned by interface implementation.

book_documents.rule: BOOK may command DOCUMENTS to render/export generic artifacts; DOCUMENTS never becomes owner of manuscript, canon, writing or publication semantics.

programming_connected_actions.rule: PROGRAMMING Website Building/Automation may request browser or connector actions only through CONNECTED_ACTIONS and cannot inherit or bypass user side-effect authority.

research_core.rule: CORE may host generic research jobs/storage/transport; RESEARCH_KNOWLEDGE owns research/knowledge/geo result and provenance semantics.

core_peer_persistence.rule: CORE storage/transaction/backup mechanics never grant CORE authority to rewrite peer semantic records.

prose_retirement.rule: PROSE is historical evidence only and may not appear as an active interface endpoint.

cross_peer_workflow_rules.orchestration: A coordinator may sequence operations but does not become semantic owner of the participating operations or stores.
cross_peer_workflow_rules.idempotency: Idempotency keys are interpreted in the provider namespace; replay never creates a second semantic transition.
cross_peer_workflow_rules.concurrency: Each provider owns version/conflict semantics for its state. Cross-peer optimistic versions are references, not a shared write lock.
cross_peer_workflow_rules.sync: Synchronous API composition cannot directly commit more than one peer's semantic store.
cross_peer_workflow_rules.events: Use owner-published facts for asynchronous propagation; consumers deduplicate and commit only consumer-owned state.
cross_peer_workflow_rules.errors: A downstream provider error remains typed to the provider even when wrapped by an upstream facade.
cross_peer_workflow_rules.cancellation: Cancellation is a provider command; a caller cannot cancel by editing provider job/state records directly.

architecture_change_required_for: adding or removing a peer system
transferring a capability or public operation between peer owners
turning Website Building into a peer
change_control.compatible_extension: A new provider-owned operation may be added inside an existing current owner/capability namespace only when it obeys this blueprint and is registered before implementation.
